title: Compute Optimization Findings
description: Output of skills/optimize-compute/scripts/evaluate_findings.py. One document per analysis run.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this schema. Bump on breaking changes.

generated_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp marking when this findings document was generated. Apply mode refuses to act on documents older than 24 hours to avoid editing files based on stale snapshots.

counts.description: Severity rollup for the executive-summary table in the report.

top_findings.description: Findings ranked by impact (severity error > warning > info; ties broken by confidence high > medium > low). Used by the report's 'Top findings' table; up to 5 entries.

workspace_host.description: Workspace URL (e.g. https://adb-1234.azuredatabricks.net). Optional - the collector emits it only when DATABRICKS_HOST is set or a response payload carries workspace_url; absent otherwise.

window.description: Time window of the underlying run-history snapshot.

insufficient_data.description: Marker (not a Finding) emitted when neither the run-count nor calendar-span gate is met. Lets the report explain why runtime rules were skipped. Null when the disjunctive gate was satisfied.

skipped_rules.description: Rules skipped because preconditions weren't met. Each entry is an object {rule_id, reason} where reason is optional and supplied when known (e.g. 'no dbt config provided', 'warehouse query history below 200 queries').

rule_id.description: Stable rule identifier. See references/findings-catalog.md for the authoritative catalog.

severity.description: info = surface for awareness; warning = should fix soon; error = wasteful or risky, fix now.

title.description: One-line human summary, used as the heading in the report.

evidence.description: Finding-specific fields supporting the diagnosis. Shape varies per rule but values must be JSON-serialisable scalars or short arrays so the report can table-render them.

summary.description: One- to three-sentence prose describing the fix.

config_delta.description: Map of config key -> { current, proposed, delete?, add? }. Each key is a dotted path into the affected config file (e.g. 'job_clusters[0].new_cluster.autoscale.max_workers'). `delete: true` signals 'remove this key' (downstream renderers should emit a deletion line rather than 'set to None'). `add: true` signals 'this key is currently absent and should be added'. The `current` / `proposed` values still convey the data when applicable. Used to render the diff block in the report.

delete.description: When true, the remediation removes this key. `proposed` will be null.

add.description: When true, the key is currently absent and the remediation adds it. `current` will be null.

affected_files.description: Repo-relative paths that would change if the remediation is applied.

apply_mode_supported.description: True only when the remediation is a mechanical single-file edit the skill can write deterministically. False for findings that need human judgement (e.g. picking a new instance type).

confidence.description: high = rule fired on direct, complete evidence (e.g. all runs in window); medium = rule fired on sampled or indirect evidence (e.g. cluster events missing for some runs); low = heuristic with known false-positive modes.

estimated_impact.description: Optional free-form impact estimate used to rank top findings in the report (e.g. '~$120/mo', '~25% DBU reduction'). Rules emit this when they can; absence is fine.

remediation.summary: Lower autoscale.max_workers from 8 to 5; peak observed across 28 runs never exceeded 4 workers.
